facts.statement: Registered suppliers receive an indicative list of eligible premises in open areas.
Suppliers must conduct further eligibility checks.
Suppliers develop project proposals and request vouchers.
A voucher project must cover at least two eligible premises.
Single connections are not eligible for GBVS.
Projects undergo commercial and value-for-money assessments.
Where current speed is below 50 Mbps, the new connection must provide at least double the existing speed.
Where current speed exceeds 50 Mbps, the new connection must provide at least 100 Mbps.
Ofcom published the Connected Nations FAQs on 11 November 2025.
Connected Nations is currently published twice a year.
The main Connected Nations report is typically released near year-end.
An interim Connected Nations update is typically released in spring.
Connected Nations reports from 2018 onward remain accessible through Ofcom.
Older Connected Nations material is available through linked National Archives pages.
The Methodology Annex explains criteria used to generate output files.
Ofcom provides separate fixed-broadband and mobile data downloads.
Speed information appears only in fixed-broadband downloads.
Fixed-broadband coverage downloads include maximum available speeds and accompany every publication.
Fixed-broadband performance downloads include active-connection speeds and local-authority full-fibre take-up.
Mobile downloads break out technology and coverage by UK, nations, local/unitary authorities and Westminster constituencies.
Ofcom revised Connected Nations data collection methodology in July 2024.
The revised method can collect from more providers but may reduce provider-specific detail.
Ofcom considers average download-speed analysis robust to local-authority level but not postcode level.
Ofcom published the Connected Nations 2025 data-download page on 19 November 2025.
